meaning_dispositions.term_phrase: retrocompact open subset U of X
meaning_dispositions.mathematical_context: Topology: retrocompact open subset U of X, whose intersections with each quasi-compact open subset V⊆X are quasi-compact; not equivalent to U itself being quasi-compact in arbitrary X.
meaning_dispositions.definition: Let X be a topological space. An open subset U⊆X is retrocompact in X if, for every quasi-compact open V⊆X, the intersection U∩V is quasi-compact. Equivalently, the inclusion U↪X is a quasi-compact map.
meaning_dispositions.mathematical_rationale: This is a named, precisely typed property of an open subset relative to its ambient space, specializing the existing independently screened quasi-compact map meaning to an inclusion. It is not the same as requiring U itself be quasi-compact without assuming X quasi-compact. The existing constructible-subset meaning uses retrocompact opens as prerequisites, and neither that construction nor the general quasi-compact-space meaning is synonymous with this named subset property. Preserve it as a specialization/contextual entry rather than force an equivalence alias.

sources.relevance: Directly checked primary source: quasi-compact map tests preimages of quasi-compact opens, and a subset is retrocompact exactly when its inclusion is quasi-compact; this gives the intersection formulation.

Quasi-compact is open-cover finite subcover without assuming Hausdorff.
U∩V is quasi-compact relative to subspace topology for each quasi-compact open V.

meaning_dispositions.definition: Let F be a field, let f∈F[T] be a nonzero polynomial, and let α belong to a field extension E/F. The element α is a repeated (multiple) root of f if (T−α)² divides f in E[T]; equivalently, f(α)=f′(α)=0.

meaning_dispositions.term_phrase: weakest topology making every evaluation map continuous
meaning_dispositions.mathematical_context: General topology: initial topology on a set X induced by maps f_i:X→(Y_i,τ_i) into topological spaces, namely the coarsest topology on X for which every f_i is continuous; it is generated by the family of all preimages f_i^{-1}[U] with U∈τ_i.
meaning_dispositions.definition: Let X be a set and (f_i:X→Y_i)_{i∈I} be maps to topological spaces (Y_i,τ_i). The initial topology on X generated by these maps is the coarsest topology on X making every f_i continuous; a subbase is {f_i^{-1}(U):i∈I,U∈τ_i}.
meaning_dispositions.mathematical_rationale: This general initial-topology construction is not identical to the screened product topology: product topology is its specialization using coordinate projections; the screened Krull topology is another specialization by Galois evaluation maps. It provides a genuine independent general definition with no requirement of injectivity or surjectivity of the maps.
